llm.summary: The skill's stated purpose (scan OpenClaw sessions and write extractions to your Feishu) matches the scripts, but the runtime prompt embeds hard-coded Feishu credentials/IDs and a default author open_id while declaring separate required env vars — an incoherent and risky mismatch that could send your data to the author's Feishu resources unless you carefully reconfigure the scripts.

dimensions.detail: The skill's name/description and scripts match: it scans OpenClaw session files, filters them, calls the OpenClaw agent to extract memories, and writes to Feishu. However the SKILL metadata/skill.json declare required env vars (FEISHU_USER_OPEN_ID, L2_APP_TOKEN, L2_TABLE_ID, L3_DOC_ID, L4_DOC_ID) but the extraction prompt embedded inside do_extract_and_write.sh hard-codes specific app_token and doc/table IDs. That mismatch (declaring env vars but instructing the agent to use hard-coded author resources) is inconsistent and unjustified for the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The runtime scripts legitimately read local OpenClaw files (sessions.json and many .jsonl session files) and send prompts to an agent; that is within scope. But the prompt injected into the AI (EXTRACT_PROMPT) explicitly instructs the agent to call OpenClaw tools with specific, hard-coded Feishu app token and table/doc IDs (author-controlled values) and a default author open_id. This effectively directs extracted session content to external Feishu endpoints not controlled by the installer unless the installer replaces those values. The scripts also default a USER_OPEN_ID to the author's ID if FEISHU_USER_OPEN_ID is not set, increasing chance of accidental leakage to the author.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec (instruction-only + shell scripts). No downloads or extracted archives; risk from install is low. The scripts expect openclaw, python3, bash, and recommend inotify-tools/jq in README, which is reasonable for the functionality.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares appropriate Feishu-related env vars as requiredEnv, which is proportional. But the actual code does not consistently use these env vars: do_extract_and_write.sh embeds explicit app_token and doc/table IDs in the prompt rather than using L2_APP_TOKEN/L2_TABLE_ID/L3_DOC_ID/L4_DOC_ID; it also sets a default FEISHU_USER_OPEN_ID to an author-owned value. Hard-coded secrets/IDs in the prompt are a high-risk mismatch with the declared env-based configuration model and are disproportionate to what's expected for the task.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (normal). The skill can be invoked autonomously by the agent (disable-model-invocation:false) — this is the platform default. Combined with the hard-coded credentials/IDs in the prompt, autonomous invocation increases the blast radius (extracted data could be sent automatically to the embedded Feishu targets).
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
Do not install or run this skill on production or with real/ sensitive session data until you address the hard-coded Feishu values. Specific actions to take before using:
- Inspect scripts (do_extract_and_write.sh and session_check.sh) and remove or replace any hard-coded app_token, table_id, and doc_id values. The prompt currently includes app_token=DdCMbcIrWawtlisBGwTcDEnznis and specific doc/table IDs — these are likely author-controlled and will route data to the author's Feishu if left unchanged.
- Set FEISHU_USER_OPEN_ID, L2_APP_TOKEN, L2_TABLE_ID, L3_DOC_ID, L4_DOC_ID in your workspace/.env and modify scripts so they use those env vars (do_extract_and_write.sh currently ignores L2_APP_TOKEN/L2_TABLE_ID/L3_DOC_ID/L4_DOC_ID in the prompt).
- Remove or change the default USER_OPEN_ID (the script falls back to an author's open_id). Ensure notifications target your own account or a safe notification sink.
- Test in an isolated environment with non-sensitive sessions to verify where data is sent. Monitor network calls and Feishu activity (rotate any tokens if they were exposed during testing).
- Prefer running the extraction with your own configured tools (or modify the prompt to instruct the agent to use env-provided tokens only). If you cannot confidently remove the hard-coded secrets, do not enable this skill on any system containing private data.
- Consider code hygiene improvements: avoid embedding secrets/IDs in prompts, and avoid relying on agents to perform outbound writes using hard-coded credentials.
If you want, I can produce a minimal patch that replaces the hard-coded IDs/tokens in the prompt with the corresponding env vars and point out exact lines to change.
